entry.title: Bangladesh’s Hidden Climate Bill: How Much Are We Losing Without Counting It?
entry.summary:
DHAKA, Bangladesh, October 22 (IPS) - Bangladesh has earned global recognition for reducing deaths from cyclones and floods. Early warning systems, cyclone shelters, embankments and community preparedness have transformed the country’s disaster response. Yet another climate crisis is receiving far less attention: the economic damage climate change is quietly inflicting on households, farmers, workers, businesses and public finances.

entry.title: What a Seawater Sample Can Tell Scientists About Ocean Health
entry.summary:
DAR ES SALAAM, Tanzania, October 22 (IPS) - A fishing boat’s catch tells only part of the story of the waters around World Heritage sites. Species that escape the net, shelter inside reefs or pass through deeper channels can go unrecorded, leaving communities and conservation officials with an incomplete picture of the marine life supporting coastal livelihoods.

Read the full story, “What a Seawater Sample Can Tell Scientists About Ocean Health”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: Were Half of Venezuela’s Oil Revenues Really Stolen? — Part I
entry.summary:
DENVER, Colorado, USA, October 21 (IPS) - If you’ve been around Venezuelans for long enough, you know that we tend to speak in superlatives. We have the best baseball players, the most beautiful beaches, the tastiest arepas, and the wickedest dictators. But even being used to the scale of our superlatives didn’t quite prepare me for what I read in the May 5 edition of The New York Times, in a story called “In Venezuela, Trump Vowed to Show Accountability. Oil Deals Linger.”

Read the full story, “Were Half of Venezuela’s Oil Revenues Really Stolen? — Part I”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: The Sámi People and Reindeer Herding – a Struggle for Sápmi’s Whole Nature
entry.summary:
SÁPMI, Norway, October 21 (IPS) - The Sámi, Europe’s last recognised Indigenous community, have faced threats to their existence throughout history. Norway last year has apologised for its forced assimilation policy following the findings of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission report, and in September 2026 Sweden has recently been told to do the same.

Read the full story, “The Sámi People and Reindeer Herding – a Struggle for Sápmi’s Whole Nature”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: As Winter Approaches, Afghanistan Faces Record Hunger and Mounting Human Rights Abuses
entry.summary:
UNITED NATIONS, October 21 (IPS) - In recent months, Afghanistan’s humanitarian crisis has severely deteriorated, with the UN reporting record-high levels of acute malnutrition and hunger. Compounded by rampant human rights violations, limited access to basic services, and persistent barriers to humanitarian aid, the UN warns that conditions could considerably worsen in the coming months.

Read the full story, “As Winter Approaches, Afghanistan Faces Record Hunger and Mounting Human Rights Abuses”, on globalissues.org →
